paragraphs: Unison sells software for the business of federal government, running from acquisitions through to budgeting. It sells to both sides of the transaction: agencies buying goods and services, and the companies bidding on and managing government contracts.

Its contract writing product is built for federal contracting professionals and aims at strict adherence to the Federal Acquisition Regulation. That product covers the whole acquisition process and is configurable to each agency's own needs. A separate set of AI modules addresses requirements development, acquisition package assembly and offer evaluation. Those modules are meant to run alongside existing systems of record rather than displace them. A third line handles cost engineering, helping agencies and contractors produce lifecycle estimates that are traceable and defendable.

The company says its contract writing product is used by 15 civilian, intelligence and defense cabinet-level agencies and dozens of defense programs. It cites a FedRAMP authorization and a DISA provisional authorization at impact level 5. The AI modules are listed as FedRAMP certified and authorized at defense impact level 4. Its cost models draw on 50 years of ongoing cost research by a dedicated team.
